utterances.text: And you said that there were guards who had no insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: They didn't have insignia, but they did have uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Some guards had military police insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But you didn't see anyone who had the insignia of the 307th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't know what that patch looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were military policemen who came from a general section opposite the church in the centre of the town of Bugojno. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: They had a command there, apparently, as far as the military police is concerned. That's what I know. It was opposite the main entrance to the church. It was across the road. That's where the building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that this area across the road in the centre of Bugojno was where the civilian police was located, the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Answer inaudible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The civilian police station, the MUP station, is opposite the hospital in the town. Opposite the hospital, near the furniture showroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: In response to a question from my colleague about the preparation for an exchange, you said that certain detainees were placed in lorries. And then you mentioned the name of Mr. Dautovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: That wasn't for the exchange. That's when they were supposed to take us to the KP Dom, the penal and correctional facility in Zenica. That's what they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Mr. Dautovic, according to you, was the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes. But as to whether he was the top commander or one of the commanders, I don't know exactly. But I know that that is what he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And all the people who surrounded him, the BH army members, would obey Mr. Dautovic's orders.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But were you in a position to see that when Mr. Dautovic issued orders his orders were obeyed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: I only saw Mr. Dautovic on that day, when we were supposed to be transported. He arrived and put an end to that transport. I only saw him in the Gimnazija on one occasion, when they took us from the basement to the room. Before they took us to the sports hall, he was present. My uncle's son was with me, and I think they, he and Dautovic, went to secondary school together. And the village he comes from and the village from which Dautovic comes too are next to each other. My aunt remained in that village and through Dautovic she managed to contact her son. She just wanted to see whether he was dead or alive, because this happened about 10 days or 12 days after I had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Dautovic was a member of the War Presidency in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Prisoners kept at the Iskra Stadium went home or they were authorised to go home with an escort; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: That was after the New Year. I think it was after the New Year. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And they would let us go two by two with a guard in order to wash ourselves. If anyone had anywhere to go to -- there was nowhere for me to go. Everything had been burnt down. My mother was staying with nuns in a monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you yourself, Mr. Gvozden, when you were at the Iskra Stadium you were not maltreated at any time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You heard about some persons who had been maltreated by people with masks on, and this happened in the course of the night.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that when the people returned. Nikica Kardelj was among them. He's one of the 21 people who went missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Gvozden, are you aware of the fact that in the area of Bugojno, since you've been living there for a long time, there were no prisons in that town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So as a soldier, you know that in order to guard prisoners of war it's necessary to find places throughout the town where the prisoners can be kept.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: It would be best to release them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Gvozden, you never knew who was in charge of the Iskra Stadium camp.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And since when you were exchanged in March 1994 and up until the time you met investigators from the OTP, you never gave a statement to anyone about what you experienced in 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN GVOZDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I thank you very much for your patience, Mr. Gvozden. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Mr. President, I would like to apologise to the interpreters. I think I have used up too much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Any questions for the other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since this testimony doesn't relate to the counts in the indictment that concern Mr. Kubura, we have no questions. But on behalf of both Defence teams, I want to take this opportunity to thank Mrs. Fleming for all her assistance and her cooperation while preparing this case and in the course of these proceedings. And we wish her all the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Are there any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, thank you for having come to The Hague to testify. You have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution and by the Defence. We wish you a good trip home. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Withopf inform us very rapidly of the schedule for the following week.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. For the next week, the Prosecution will call seven witnesses: One on Monday, one on Tuesday, two on Wednesday, two on Thursday, and two on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber would like to thank everyone, and I will see you next week at the hearing, which will commence as usual at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st of March, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.57 p.m.,
